title: DC-area forecast: Scattered showers possible Friday before a nice Saturday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Evening temperatures fall back through the 80s. Humidity trends higher again later this evening and overnight with lows around 70 to 75.

What’s next? Mostly cloudy Friday with scattered afternoon showers possible. Nice start to the weekend on Saturday. Shower or storm potential could return Sunday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Just a small chance of a stray evening shower. Under partly cloudy skies, overnight lows should fall to around 70 to 75. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Partly to mostly cloudy skies should keep temperatures down somewhat, with highs mainly in the low to mid-80s. We'll be watching storms to the northwest to see how they travel toward the area. Some scattered showers and storm are possible during the afternoon into evening. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Scattered showers and a storm remain a risk into the evening, perhaps until a couple hours after sunset. Lows range from the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

More typical August conditions through the weekend. Highs mainly in the mid-80s on Saturday with mostly sunny skies and somewhat lower humidity. Perhaps a touch toastier and more humid Sunday as highs reach around the mid-80s to near 90. Our late-day shower and storm threat may also return Sunday. Confidence: Medium

A chance of a few showers or storms may persist into Monday as readings rise to around 90. Highs in the mid-80s to near 90 Tuesday, and it could be less humid with seemingly low storm chances for now. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Sun rules but it's also hotter than it should be which isn't fun by mid-August. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 13

Extreme heat in 2016 sent temperatures to 101 degrees with record-warm nights, followed by powerful thunderstorms that knocked out power and brought heavy rain.
